context: It's your first evening near your host's village and the only shop still open is the konbini. Today: getting your bento heated, saying no to a bag, and paying.

phrases.jp: これ、{温めて|あたためて|to heat up, warm|3}もらえますか。
phrases.note: Usually staff ask you first: {温|あたた}めますか? Just say はい、お{願|ねが}いします.
Bags cost 3–5 yen. When asked {袋|ふくろ}はご{利用|りよう}ですか, a soft {大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}です also means "no thanks".

phrases.en: Could you put in some chopsticks?
phrases.jp: お{箸|はし|chopsticks|4}を{付けて|つけて|to add, include|4}もらえますか。
phrases.note: You'll hear お{箸|はし|chopsticks|4}おつけしますか? Chopsticks, spoons and straws are free but often only on request.

phrases.jp: {別々|べつべつ|separately|3}に{入|い}れてください。
phrases.note: Handy when hot food and cold drinks or ice cream would go in the same bag.

phrases.en: Can we stop by the konbini for a sec?
phrases.jp: ちょっとコンビニ{寄って|よって|to drop by|3}もいい？
phrases.note: {寄|よ}る = drop in on the way. Very common with friends on a walk or a drive.

dialogue_setting: At the till of a konbini, late evening.

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.jp: お{弁当|べんとう|boxed meal|4}、{温めます|あたためます|to heat up, warm|3}か。
dialogue.en: Shall I heat up your bento?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: はい、お{願|ねが}いします。

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.jp: ポイントカードはお{持ち|もち|(honorific) do you have|3}ですか。
dialogue.en: Do you have a points card?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: いえ、{大丈夫|だいじょうぶ|(here) I'm fine, no thanks|4}です。

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.jp: お{支払い|しはらい|payment|3}は{現金|げんきん|cash|3}ですか。

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: いえ、ICカードでお{願|ねが}いします。

kanji.where: On yellow or red stickers on bento, onigiri and bread close to their date, often in the evening. 2{割引|わりびき} = 20% off; 50{円引|えんび}き = 50 yen off.
kanji.related: Related: {半額|はんがく} half price, {消費期限|しょうひきげん} use-by date.
kanji.breakdown: {割引|わりびき}: 割 cut, divide + 引 pull, take away → part of the price is cut off.

tip.title: Eating in changes the tax
tip.body: At the till you may hear {店内|てんない|inside the shop|2}でお{召し上がり|めしあがり|to eat (honorific)|2}ですか (Eating here?). Food to take away is taxed at 8%, but eating in the konbini's eat-in corner is 10%, so say {持|も}ち{帰|かえ}りです if you're taking it away. Konbini also have free toilets, ATMs that take foreign cards, and copy machines that print documents from your phone.

challenge.prompt: Tell the clerk you don't need a bag, and ask if you can pay by card.
challenge.model_answer: {袋|ふくろ|bag|4}はいりません。カードで{払|はら}えますか。
challenge.explanation: {袋|ふくろ}はいりません: いる here is 要る 'to need', so いりません = I don't need it (not 'there isn't'). カードで: で marks the means. {払|はら}える is the can-form of {払|はら}う, so the whole thing is 'Can I pay by card?'

vocab.note: Plastic shopping bag = レジ{袋|ぶくろ}.
Also for paying separately: {別々|べつべつ}でお{願|ねが}いします.

kanji_study.kun: あたた(かい)・あたた(める)

extras.title: What the clerk might say
extras.title_jp: {店員|てんいん}さんの{言葉|ことば}
extras.intro: Fast, polite set phrases you'll hear at every till.

items.jp: {袋|ふくろ|bag|4}はご{利用|りよう|use (polite ご〜ですか = do you need)|3}ですか。
{年齢確認|ねんれいかくにん|age verification|1}のボタンを{押|お}してください。
items.en: Please press the age check button.
items.note: For alcohol and cigarettes: tap the screen to confirm you're over 20.

items.jp: レシートはご{利用|りよう|use (polite ご〜ですか = do you need)|3}ですか。
こちらにタッチしてください。

extras.title: More than a shop
extras.title_jp: コンビニでできること
extras.intro: Konbini are mini service centres. Ask for these at the till.

items.jp: {コピー機|コピーき|photocopier|2}を{使|つか}いたいんですが。
items.en: I'd like to use the copy machine.

items.jp: これ、ここから{送|おく}れますか。
items.en: Can I send this from here?
items.note: Most konbini accept parcels ({宅急便|たっきゅうびん|courier parcel delivery|2}).

items.jp: トイレをお{借り|かり|to borrow (humble お〜する)|3}してもいいですか。
